description: Global living/revived unarmed-combat style database for VirtualProGrapplerMMA. Ratings are game-design starting points, not claims of real-world superiority.

styles.name: Boxing
styles.notes: Modern gloved boxing; elite hand striking, footwork and defense.

styles.name: Bare-Knuckle Boxing
styles.notes: Bare-knuckle rules emphasize hand durability, clinch fighting and compact punching.

styles.name: Catch Wrestling
styles.notes: Submission-oriented wrestling descended from Lancashire catch-as-catch-can.

styles.name: Lancashire Wrestling
styles.notes: Traditional English catch-as-catch-can wrestling.

styles.name: Cornish Wrestling
styles.notes: Jacket wrestling tradition from Cornwall.

styles.name: Scottish Backhold Wrestling
styles.notes: Standing backhold wrestling; falling first loses.

styles.name: Irish Collar-and-Elbow
styles.notes: Historic Irish standing jacket-and-grip wrestling with modern revival.

styles.name: Savate
styles.notes: French kickboxing emphasizing precision, footwear-based kicking and range.

styles.name: Judo
styles.notes: Throwing and grappling art founded by Jigoro Kano.

styles.name: Japanese Jujutsu
styles.notes: Umbrella category for living Japanese jujutsu schools.

styles.name: Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu
styles.notes: Ground-focused submission grappling developed in Brazil from judo/jujutsu.

styles.name: Luta Livre Esportiva
styles.notes: Brazilian no-gi submission wrestling.

styles.name: Vale Tudo
styles.notes: Brazilian minimal-rules mixed fighting tradition.

styles.name: Capoeira
styles.notes: Afro-Brazilian martial art emphasizing deceptive movement, kicks and sweeps.

styles.name: Huka-Huka
styles.notes: Indigenous Brazilian wrestling practiced among peoples of the Xingu.

styles.name: Sport Sambo
styles.notes: Jacket grappling sport blending regional wrestling and judo influences.

styles.name: Combat Sambo
styles.notes: Combat form of Sambo integrating strikes and submissions.

styles.name: Freestyle Wrestling
styles.notes: Olympic wrestling allowing attacks to the legs.

styles.name: Greco-Roman Wrestling
styles.notes: Olympic upper-body wrestling; leg attacks are prohibited.

styles.name: American Folkstyle Wrestling
styles.notes: US scholastic/collegiate wrestling emphasizing control and escapes.

styles.name: Sumo
styles.notes: Japanese ring-out and throw wrestling.

styles.name: Shoot Wrestling
styles.notes: Japanese submission-fighting lineage that grew from professional wrestling.

styles.name: Shooto
styles.notes: Japanese mixed combat sport founded by Satoru Sayama.

styles.name: Pancrase-Style Hybrid
styles.notes: Open-palm striking and submission-heavy Japanese hybrid ruleset.

styles.name: Shotokan Karate
styles.notes: Linear karate emphasizing distance, timing and decisive attacks.

styles.name: Kyokushin Karate
styles.notes: Full-contact knockdown karate known for body conditioning and powerful kicks.

styles.name: Ashihara Karate
styles.notes: Sabaki-oriented knockdown karate.

styles.name: Enshin Karate
styles.notes: Sabaki karate with grabs, sweeps and throws.

styles.name: Kudo
styles.notes: Japanese mixed combat sport combining knockdown karate, judo-style grappling and head-protected striking.

styles.name: Muay Thai
styles.notes: Thai eight-limb striking with strong clinch fighting.

styles.name: Muay Boran
styles.notes: Umbrella term for pre-modern Thai fighting methods still practiced today.

styles.name: Lethwei
styles.notes: Burmese bare-knuckle striking allowing headbutts.

styles.name: Pradal Serey / Kun Khmer
styles.notes: Cambodian ring striking art with elbows, knees and clinch.

styles.name: Bokator
styles.notes: Cambodian traditional martial art with striking and grappling components.

styles.name: Sanda / Sanshou
styles.notes: Chinese full-contact kickboxing with throws and catches.

styles.name: Shuai Jiao
styles.notes: Chinese jacket wrestling emphasizing fast throws.

styles.name: Wing Chun
styles.notes: Southern Chinese close-range striking system.

styles.name: Bajiquan
styles.notes: Chinese style known for explosive short-range power and elbows.

styles.name: Choy Li Fut
styles.notes: Southern Chinese striking art using wide circular hand techniques and kicks.

styles.name: Hung Gar
styles.notes: Southern Chinese system emphasizing rooted stances and powerful hand techniques.

styles.name: Taekwondo
styles.notes: Korean kicking art and Olympic combat sport.

styles.name: Taekkyeon
styles.notes: Traditional Korean martial art with rhythmic footwork, kicks and trips.

styles.name: Ssireum
styles.notes: Korean belt wrestling.

styles.name: Hapkido
styles.notes: Korean martial art combining kicks, throws and joint locks.

styles.name: Tang Soo Do
styles.notes: Korean striking art influenced by karate and indigenous traditions.

styles.name: Yaw-Yan
styles.notes: Filipino kickboxing system known for powerful rotational kicks.

styles.name: Panantukan / Suntukan
styles.notes: Filipino empty-hand boxing concepts associated with FMA.

styles.name: Dumog
styles.notes: Filipino grappling/wrestling methods.

styles.name: Sikaran
styles.notes: Filipino kicking art.

styles.name: Pencak Silat
styles.notes: Large family of Southeast Asian martial traditions; this entry models common unarmed competition/self-defense concepts.

styles.name: Silat Olahraga
styles.notes: Sport silat ruleset focused on strikes, catches, sweeps and throws.

styles.name: Vovinam
styles.notes: Vietnamese martial art combining striking, throws and locks.

styles.name: Vat Co Truyen
styles.notes: Traditional Vietnamese wrestling.

styles.name: Krav Maga
styles.notes: Modern self-defense system; game representation limited to unarmed techniques.

styles.name: KAPAP
styles.notes: Israeli close-combat system; unarmed subset only.

styles.name: Systema
styles.notes: Russian martial-art family emphasizing relaxation, movement and adaptive response.

styles.name: Army Hand-to-Hand Combat
styles.notes: Russian military-derived competitive hand-to-hand system.

styles.name: Kurash
styles.notes: Uzbek jacket wrestling.

styles.name: Alysh
styles.notes: Central Asian belt wrestling.

styles.name: Kazakh Kuresi
styles.notes: Kazakh traditional wrestling.

styles.name: Bökh
styles.notes: Mongolian traditional wrestling.

styles.name: Pehlwani / Kushti
styles.notes: South Asian traditional wrestling.

styles.name: Malla-Yuddha
styles.notes: Living/revived South Asian grappling tradition.

styles.name: Kalaripayattu — Unarmed
styles.notes: Unarmed subset of Kalaripayattu.

styles.name: Musti-Yuddha
styles.notes: Traditional South Asian fist-fighting lineage; surviving practice is limited.

styles.name: Yağlı Güreş
styles.notes: Turkish oil wrestling.

styles.name: Karakucak
styles.notes: Traditional Turkish free wrestling.

styles.name: Glíma
styles.notes: Icelandic wrestling tradition.

styles.name: Schwingen
styles.notes: Swiss breeches wrestling.

styles.name: Gouren
styles.notes: Breton jacket wrestling.

styles.name: Laamb / Senegalese Wrestling
styles.notes: Senegalese wrestling; professional forms may include striking.

styles.name: Nuba Wrestling
styles.notes: Traditional wrestling of Nuba communities.

styles.name: Dambe
styles.notes: Hausa striking sport centered on a dominant wrapped punching hand.

styles.name: Moraingy
styles.notes: Malagasy bare-fist striking tradition.

styles.name: Engolo
styles.notes: Angolan combat game/martial tradition associated with inverted and kicking movement.

styles.name: Lucha Canaria
styles.notes: Canarian jacket/belt wrestling.

styles.name: Lucha Leonesa
styles.notes: Traditional Spanish belt wrestling.

styles.name: Modern Pankration
styles.notes: Modern sport revival inspired by ancient pankration.

styles.name: Combat Hapkido
styles.notes: Modern self-defense system derived from Hapkido.

styles.name: American Kenpo
styles.notes: American Kenpo/Kenpo Karate family.

styles.name: American Kickboxing
styles.notes: Full-contact American kickboxing tradition.

styles.name: Mixed Martial Arts
styles.notes: Modern mixed martial arts; broad baseline rather than a regional style.
